adjudication.claim_boundary: Stage 5 tests one positive lean policy construction, one unchanged strong flat baseline, and a pre-registered scale matrix. A channel that prevents a scored failure is requirement-sensitive on this matrix only. Full-vs-baseline results remain directional evidence, not a general Ghost-superiority claim. Lean Ghost still stores the full Ghost runtime state; this experiment adjudicates decision-path simplification, not production package deletion or memory savings.

lean_semantics: utility + goals + beliefs action scoring; value contribution disabled; delayed recall influence disabled; full Ghost storage retained
next_experiment: Adjudicate whether the evidence supports retaining decision channels, simplifying policy, or increasing adversarial scale. Do not modify production subsystems solely from this one matrix.
stage5_non_claim: Stage 5 does not establish general Ghost superiority, realism, intelligence, uniqueness, or production necessity. Lean Ghost retains full runtime storage, so decision-path findings do not prove package deletion or memory savings. Requirement-sensitive value/recall findings apply only to the scored Stage-5 requirements.
stage5_supported_claim: Stage 5 can determine whether the Stage-4 decision-path simplification remains behaviorally sufficient on the frozen replay and broader pre-registered workload, and can record directional Full-Ghost-vs-baseline behavior, failure onset, and state burden on that workload.
